newsitem.title: USA: AMA approves standardized physician accreditation.
newsitem.headline: AMA approves standardized physician accreditation.

text.p: The American Medical Association, the nation's largest doctors' group, said Tuesday it has approved a standard accreditation process for physicians to help consumers make informed decisions.
The American Medical Accreditation Programme, intended to streamline credentialing procedures used by various health plans, was approved by doctors attending an AMA policy meeting.

The organisation said procedures for credentialing and office site review would be developed with input from physicians. It said the new accreditation would retain "some of the current credentialing procedures used by states, localities and speciality medical societies."
"The plan is expected to help consumers make more informed decisions about their physicians and ease administrative burdens on physicians," the AMA said in a statement.
